claims.text: Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi exhibits inherent local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi produces a broad distribution of dislocation activation thresholds.
A broad distribution of dislocation activation thresholds delays the onset of plasticity during dynamic compression.
A broad distribution of dislocation activation thresholds enhances work hardening during dynamic loading.
Substituting a small fraction of one constituent with an element of slightly different atomic size will reduce overall lattice distortion.
Reducing lattice distortion will narrow the distribution of dislocation activation thresholds.
Narrowing the distribution of dislocation activation thresholds will lower flow stress.
Narrowing the distribution of dislocation activation thresholds will reduce strain-rate sensitivity.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 and ambient temperature, the unmodified alloy will have higher flow stress than the modified alloy with reduced lattice distortion.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 and ambient temperature, the unmodified alloy will exhibit greater strain-rate sensitivity than the modified alloy.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 and ambient temperature, the unmodified alloy will exhibit stronger work hardening than the modified alloy.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi under high-strain-rate loading near 10^3 s^-1 at ambient temperature.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under quasi-static loading.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when phase stability is compromised.
High-resolution X-ray diffraction strain mapping and local atomic-displacement statistics can quantify the proposed local lattice distortion.
The compositional modification could introduce local phase changes or chemical ordering that independently influence dynamic mechanical behavior.

contradictions.description: The design describes the modified sample as having reduced lattice distortion, but the falsification rule allows the modified sample to have a distortion distribution similar to the baseline. Similar distortion would indicate failure to manipulate the proposed mediator, not a decisive falsification of its mechanical role.
